questions.knowledge_point: The Cartesian Equation of an Ellipse
questions.problem:
Determine the Cartesian equation of the ellipse

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,0\le \theta <2\pi .
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the Cartesian equation of the ellipse, we need to eliminate the parameter $\theta .$ We can do this using the Pythagorean theorem.

By isolating the $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ term in the $x$-equation and squaring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{x}{2} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{{2}^{2}} & ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{4} & ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

By isolating the $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ term in the $y$-equation and squaring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ {y}^{2} & ={sin}^{2}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

 

Adding the two equations and using ${cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+{y}^{2} & ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1.\end{aligned}
$$

So the Cartesian equation of the ellipse is

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+{y}^{2}=1.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: The Parametric Equations of an Ellipse Centered at a General Point
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070244/assets/14d1fc5a92c28cc7f84c1ec23929701f1aca67b1a15d6113fa83f1428354fc11.png)

Consider the ellipse centered at $(3,-1)$ with horizontal radius $2$ and vertical radius $3,$ as shown above. Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $\theta \in [0,2\pi ),$  traverse the ellipse once in the counterclockwise direction starting at the point $A(5,-1)?$
questions.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at the point $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +h,\,y=b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +k,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

Under this parametrization, the ellipse is traversed once in the counterclockwise direction, starting from $(h+a,k).$

In our case, the ellipse is centered at the point $(3,-1),$ $a=2$ and $b=3.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the ellipse are 

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +3,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -1,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070244/assets/48c5190fc4f45f4bf3e76a56977339559ceb30ca90a41411d3bc4df2362b0787.png)

The semi-ellipse above is defined by the parametric equations 

$$
x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $\theta ?$
questions.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

In our case, $a=4$ and $b=3.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the *full* ellipse are

$$
x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a semi-ellipse, we associate the parameter $\theta $ with the central angle formed by a point $(x,y)$ on the elipse and the $x$-axis. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070244/assets/546b9f72124a7eb05877db3600e40b5772404a1a3378de67cfbe3320c78ac2ba.png)

We can see that if we restrict $\theta $ to $[0,\pi ]$, we get the semi-ellipse.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the semi-ellipse are 

$$
x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,\pi ].
$$

questions.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at the point $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +h,\,y=b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +k,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).

$$

questions.knowledge_point: The Cartesian Equation of an Ellipse
questions.problem:
Determine the Cartesian equation of the ellipse

$$
x=3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -5,\,y=6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -2,\,0\le \theta <2\pi .
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the Cartesian equation of the ellipse, we need to eliminate the parameter $\theta .$ We can do this using the Pythagorean theorem.

By isolating the $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ term in the $x$-equation and squaring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -5 \\ \frac{x+5}{3} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{(x+5)^{2}}{{3}^{2}} & ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{(x+5)^{2}}{9} & ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta ,\end{aligned}
$$

By isolating the $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ term in the $y$-equation and squaring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -2 \\ \frac{y+2}{6} & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{(y+2)^{2}}{{6}^{2}} & ={sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{(y+2)^{2}}{36} & ={sin}^{2}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

 
Adding the two equations and using ${cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x+5)^{2}}{9}+\frac{(y+2)^{2}}{36} & ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1.\end{aligned}
$$

So the Cartesian equation of the ellipse is

$$
\frac{(x+5)^{2}}{9}+\frac{(y+2)^{2}}{36}=1.
$$
